newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's 28-day Cetes rates seen below 18 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's 28-day Cetes rates seen below 18 pct.

text.p: Mexico's bellwether 28-day Cetes rate could dip below its long-term support level of 18 percent at the next primary treasury bill auction, Ixe bank said in a report released on Sunday.
"For the primary auction this week we are looking at a general decline, with the 28-day Cetes rates falling below its long-term support (18 percent)," Ixe wrote.

It said the decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve to leave interest rates in the U.S. unchanged last week as well as lower-than-expected inflation for the first two weeks of May in Mexico has allowed interest rates in Mexico's secondary money market to fall to new recent lows.

It also said there is the possibility of a rebound in Mexican interest rates due to pre-election nervousness before the July 6 mid-term votes, pressure on the exchange rate, and a move out of long-term paper to short-term paper or into cash.
Ixe said it is almost a certainty that inflation for May will be below 1.0 percent. For the first two week of May the consumer price index rose 0.48 percent, the central bank said last week.
The 28-day Cetes rate fell 84 basis points to 18.07 percent at the primary auction last week.
